candidates: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC)
SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome)
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene
champion: SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas

raw.champion: SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas
raw.rationale: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, as revealed by whole-exome sequencing, along with the clinical presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules and family history of similar lesions, supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC)
rejected.why: While similar, the specific genetic mutation points more directly to a SUFU-related condition

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This option does not account for the hereditary aspect or the specific genetic findings

rejected.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome)
rejected.why: Gorlin syndrome typically includes a broader range of features such as palmar or plantar pits, jaw cysts, and other systemic manifestations not present in this case

rejected.label: Basal cell nevus syndrome
rejected.why: Another term for Gorlin syndrome, which does not fit as well due to the absence of characteristic features like palmar pits and jaw cysts
